items.title: Notes for agents: a person marks tiles or meshes with a note, an agent works it, and the sign goes away
items.goal: A person selects one or more tiles or placed meshes and leaves a note for an agent. The note stands in the viewport as a small 3D construction sign; clicking it opens the note to read and edit. An agent lists open notes over MCP, does the work through ordinary operations and resolves the note, and its sign disappears while the change it made stays on screen. Resolved notes stay on record, so what has been worked can still be read.
acceptance: a note left on two placements and one tile is saved with the map's project and survives an editor restart
each open note shows one construction sign above its targets, and a resolved note shows none
clicking a sign opens its note; an edit to the text is saved and is one undo step
an agent over MCP lists the open notes with their targets, makes the change, resolves the note naming the operations it ran, and the sign is gone within a second while the change is on screen
resolved notes are listed with what resolved them, and an undo of the resolve brings the sign back
items.evidence: Owner's request 2026-10-28, with the focus in docs/loop/focus.md. Design defaults, so no pass has to stop for them: notes are data in the game's project beside the map they mark (one file per map, written like the map, hot-reloaded through bevy_grimoire_core::live::FileWatch); a note has an id, its targets (placement ids and cells), its text, open or resolved, and on resolve the operation ids and one line of what changed; the sign is orange and white, about knee height on the map's scale, standing above the centre of its targets and never hiding them; every note change is a registered operation with undo, reachable from both the UI and MCP. The sign starts as a mesh built from Bevy primitives; a golem-made .glb replaces it only when the owner supplies one (AGENTS.md: meshes come from golem, not from this repo). A new keys::Action needs a row in the protected keys.rs census (see S3.7): ship click and button entry first and log a key as blocked rather than editing the census. 2026-10-28: moved to GitHub issues #89-#95 (label `owner`), which the owner approved as the plan and which extend it: drag a rectangle or Shift-click pieces, a box at the selection, Send, any MCP agent claims with a lease, a fence of area plus one cell, ask-first rules, review with Keep or Undo this note, and every note's history. Work the issues, not these steps; S4.1 stays the core they extend.

items.title: Hot reload: every file the editor writes reaches a running program by a declared path
items.goal: A new kind of file cannot ship without a declared reload class, every editor write is atomic, a bad file never replaces a good state, runtime state keeps its identity across a reload, and the editor shows each file's reload state
acceptance: docs/guide/reload-contract.md lists every kind the editor writes, with class and lifetime
every_written_kind_has_a_reload_class and the_restart_list_only_shrinks fail when a kind is added without a class or to Restart without the list
a reload that does not parse keeps the last good state and reports a verdict per kind
the editor shows each file's reload state
items.evidence: Issues #198 to #204, labelled owner and hot-reload; the focus puts them first (437eece, d8f9566). H2 (pass 165, 2026-10-31, closed #199): bevy_grimoire_core::atomic_file is the one write path (unique hidden temp beside the target, flushed, renamed, directory flushed); 19 plain writes moved onto it; core tests/atomic_writes.rs, atomic_file_contract.rs and the ratchet atomic_writes_only.rs. H3 slice 1 (pass 166, 2026-10-31, #200 stays open): core reload_check::check parses a file as its kind (18 of 33 kinds) and names the file and the field (serde_path_to_error, only after a refusal); Verdict v2 adds seq and per-file kinds (applied or refused); project_data::verdicts gives one entry per file the game's load reads; the game writes one verdict per edit; grimoire_state.game and the journal carry them.
